top_candidates.subject: [SimpleLoopUnswitch] Generalize the notion of trivial unswitching (#193989)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: SimpleLoopUnswitch generalizes 'trivial unswitching' to handle invariant branches that either exit a loop or bypass the loop latch without duplicating the loop body. The implementation adds a latch-rewrite path that redirects a latch successor to the unique loop exit when the latch has no side effects and the loop is provably finite, then updates PHIs, DominatorTree, and MemorySSA (via MSSAU) to keep CFG and memory-dependence structures consistent. This significantly expands the control-flow shapes considered trivial unswitchable and introduces new verification-sensitive logic around loop exits, PHIs, and incremental analysis updates.
Mechanisms: trivial loop unswitching generalization; latch-bypass CFG rewrite; PHI node rewiring for unique latch exits; DominatorTree incremental updates; MemorySSA update application via MSSAU; finite-loop proof using SCEV max backedge count
Touched symbols: SimpleLoopUnswitch.cpp; unswitchTrivialBranch; areLoopExitPHIsLoopInvariant; Loop::getLoopLatch; Loop::getUniqueLatchExitBlock; SCEV::getConstantMaxBackedgeTakenCount; MSSAU->applyUpdates; DominatorTree::applyUpdates
Risk relevance: directly mutates CFG edges and relies on correct DT/MemorySSA updates, a common source of verification assertions; introduces new unswitch cases involving latch edges and loop exits, increasing control-flow complexity; checks for side-effect-free latches and finite loops to avoid semantic changes; mistakes here can cause miscompiles or verifier failures; touches MemorySSA-backed scalar loop transformation logic, which is high-risk for clobber-walker assertions
Build risk: new control-flow handling adds many new regression tests and broad optimizer surface area; uses SCEV, LoopInfo, DominatorTree, and MemorySSA update plumbing together, increasing integration fragility; adds new test file and changes phase-ordering expectations across several targets
